what_happened: The job to add a defaults entry ("criteria check behavior, protections tested as roo...") ended rejected. Its final verdict was fail, with two major findings from the verifier. First, an edit to crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md joined two bullets into one line, so the 'deliverables:' instruction stopped being its own bullet. Second, the CHANGELOG entry (Unreleased / Added) said the reader prompt names the protection rule, and it does not. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. The only problems are the two findings.
cause: Nothing in the job compares the finished diff against what was intended. A prompt file is edited as free text, and no check confirms that only the intended lines changed or that the structure survived (each instruction still its own bullet). The changelog text is written from the intent, not from what the diff contains, so a claim like 'the reader prompt names the rule' is never tied to the file. The only review is the verifier at the end, so both slips surface as a rejection and not as an earlier fix. Acceptance criteria also seem to cover the new defaults entry, not the collateral files.
prevention: Add a pre-verification check that runs on every job touching prompts or docs. (1) For prompt files, show the diff and fail if any changed hunk modifies lines outside the intended edit, or if the bullet or line structure changes where no change was intended (for example, a line count or bullet-marker count that drops). (2) For each new CHANGELOG line, require a named reference to the file and the string it asserts, and have the check confirm that string exists in the changed files, so a claim like 'the reader prompt names the protection rule' fails when reader.md lacks it. Run it before the job is submitted for verification, and send failures back to the worker.
proposed_request: Repair the rejected job 20261015-095214-y8kr. (1) In crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md, restore the 'deliverables:' instruction as its own bullet on its own line, so the file differs from its previous version only by the intended change. (2) Make the CHANGELOG.md entry under Unreleased / Added true. Either add the protection rule to the reader prompt as its own bullet, or reword the entry to say only what the diff does. Keep the new defaults entry (criteria check behavior, protections tested as roots). Outcome: the diff touches only the defaults entry, the reader prompt and the changelog line. Every claim in the changelog entry can be found in the changed files. The reader prompt keeps one instruction per bullet.
